title: Portrait of the Alter Rebbe
description: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi (1745–1812), founder of the Chabad-Lubavitch movement and author of the Tanya. The Alter Rebbe established the philosophical and spiritual framework of Chabad Chassidus. His son, the Mitteler Rebbe, settled in Lubavitch around 1813, making it the center of the movement.

title: Portrait of the Mitteler Rebbe
description: Rabbi Dovber Schneuri (1773–1827), second Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch and son of the Alter Rebbe. The Mitteler Rebbe settled in Lubavitch around 1813, establishing the village as the seat of Chabad leadership for the next century. He led the movement until his passing in Niezhin in 1827.

title: Portrait of the Tzemach Tzedek
description: Portrait of Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn (1789–1866), the third Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch, known as the Tzemach Tzedek. He led the movement from 1827 until his passing in Lubavitch in 1866. His Ohel in Lubavitch remains one of the primary destinations for Chabad pilgrims worldwide.

title: Portrait of the Rebbe Maharash
description: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn (1834–1882), fourth Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch and seventh son of the Tzemach Tzedek. He led the movement from Lubavitch, where he is also buried alongside his father. Known for his teaching of 'l'chatchilah ariber' — approach every challenge from above — which became a hallmark of the Chabad ethos.
notes: Historical photograph; original in Chabad archives.

title: Portrait of the Rebbe Rashab
description: Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn (1860–1920), fifth Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch and son of the Rebbe Maharash. In 1897 he founded Yeshivah Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch — the first yeshiva to combine deep Talmud study with intensive study of Chassidus. He left Lubavitch in 1915 due to World War I and passed away in Rostov-on-Don in 1920.
credit: Public domain (Russian Federation Civil Code, Art. 1259)

title: Portrait of the Frierdiker Rebbe
description: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (1880–1950), sixth Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch, born in Lubavitch. In 1922 he delivered his last Maamar (Chassidic discourse) in Russia in the shul adjacent to the Ohel in Lubavitch. He subsequently led Chabad from Riga, Warsaw, and — after surviving the Holocaust — from New York, laying the foundation for the worldwide Chabad movement.

title: Portrait of the Lubavitcher Rebbe
description: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson (1902–1994), seventh and most recent Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch. Son-in-law of the Frierdiker Rebbe, he accepted the nesius (leadership) in 1951. Under his direction, Chabad expanded to over 100 countries and thousands of communities. He is widely regarded as one of the most influential Jewish leaders of the 20th century.

title: Lyubavichi Village — Aerial View
description: Contemporary photograph of the village of Lyubavichi (Lubavitch) from above, showing the rural landscape of the Smolensk region. The village, once a thriving Jewish center with over 1,600 Jewish residents, today has a population of approximately 460. The forests and rivers surrounding the village are unchanged from the time of the Rebbeim.

title: Lubavitch Cemetery — Ohel and Grounds
description: The grounds of the historic Lubavitch cemetery, spanning approximately 70 by 150 meters at the western edge of the village. The cemetery contains the graves of Chabad Rebbeim, Rebbetzins, and generations of the Jewish community. After decades of neglect during the Soviet period and the devastation of the Holocaust, the cemetery has been systematically restored beginning in 2018.

title: The Schneerson House in Lyubavichi
description: The Schneerson House — a building purchased in 1989 and registered in the name of the Lubavitcher Rebbe. Located in Lyubavichi, it serves as a guest house for pilgrims and a small museum documenting the history of Chabad in Lubavitch.
